text.text_excerpt: Let me say that I really enjoyed my stay here. I'll talk about the room I stayed in first. Our double room was spacious and comfortable. The decor is a feast for the senses. I loved the old school, fully stocked bar and SMEG refrigerator. Found even some Wiseacre brews in it which is one my home town's brewery. Cool. I thought the bathrooms were fine. Loved the black tiles, the splash of marble for the step in and the deep Amazon, high lacquered green trim paint mixed with the grey walls. Sumptuous feeling but still modern. The room itself had hefty, wood interior shutters to close at night to block out the light in addition to the blocking shade. It got blackout dark in our room which wa...

My new favorite hotel in New Orleans. I'm an Omni loyalty guest at the highest level, yet I'll never again stay at one of the three Omnis in town (even with the promise of upgrades) because now that I've stayed at the Ace, I am ruined. Ruined, I tell you. A stuffy corporate cookie cutter room just isn't going to ever cut it again when the promise of dark walls, vintage fridges and turntables with charmingly worn records are waiting for me! I believe the room I stayed in was a medium size (ie, not the smallest, not the biggest, not a suite). I absolutely adored it and wished I was staying longer than merely one night. Comfy bed, delicious bath products, space for dancing... What a unique s...

Hands down the cutest hotel I have ever stayed at in New Orleans and in all honesty Ace will now make it tremendously tough to book a room at any other space going forward. We were originally booked in at another small cute boutique hotel for a few days but when we checked the weather we knew wanted a pool. One of the first things we checked out after checking in, and it did not disappoint. The Saturday pool scene at the Ace rooftop and bar Alto rival any pool scene you'd want to be at in any city/state. I immediately said this space screams summer.
